subject: Deployment mode follow-up — latency & throughput thresholds
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Shaw <ethan@fastlane.ai>, FastLane Analytics Procurement <procurement@fastlane.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 02 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Deployment mode follow-up — latency & throughput thresholds

Ethan / procurement team — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we can align on whether Hosted API, Redwood Dedicated, or Private VPC is the right path for FastLane. Attaching the traffic extract you shared (fastlane_qps_profile.csv) and a short matrix that maps decision drivers to options (redwood-hosted-vs-dedicated-matrix.pdf).

Summary of what you described:
- Typical steady-state: ~120 qps
- Peak microbursts: up to ~350 qps for ~1–3 minute windows, multiple times per hour
- Desired latency targets: p50 ~80ms, p99 target <= 250ms
- Model: customer-facing recommendation model (13B, KV cache friendly)
- Regulated fields: user identifiers/anonymized telemetry (ok under standard Hosted TOS for now, but procurement pushed the option for Private later)

Initial recommendation (short):
- If you need consistent p99 <= 250ms under sustained 200–350 qps, Redwood Dedicated is the conservative choice — dedicated GPU pool to guarantee concurrency and predictable tail latency.
- Hosted API + workload-aware batching + KV/prefix caching can hit p50 easily and may meet p99 for short, infrequent bursts, but it’s a risk under repeated sustained peaks; cost is typically lower initially.
- Private VPC/on-prem is primarily driven by compliance/audit constraints — we can scope if procurement needs that later.

Proposed pilot approach:
1) 48–72 hour microbenchmark on Dedicated with your recorded traffic replay (we’ll run a canary at burst windows) — objective: validate p99 at your 350 qps bursts and capture cost envelope.
2) Parallel Hosted tuning trial (same traffic, smaller scale) to quantify what batching/caching buys you and the failure/fallback behavior.
3) Deliver a comparison: latency curves (p50/p95/p99), cost per 1M tokens, and an operational playbook (fallback routes, autoscale knobs).

Action items / asks:
- Ethan: confirm you can share the 1–2 hour high-resolution traffic sample (we already have the CSV; a raw request log with timestamps is ideal).
- Procurement: share approval window for a short Dedicated pilot and any contractual hurdles we should know about (SLA/PO timelines).
- Ben / Lauren: can you confirm pilot resource availability next week and a preliminary pricing band for a 2–4 week committed pilot?

I’m free to run the bench next Tue–Thu; propose we book a 30 minute follow-up mid-day Friday to review pilot plan and sign-off.

Attachments (stubs): fastlane_qps_profile.csv, redwood-hosted-vs-dedicated-matrix.pdf

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
From: Ethan Shaw <ethan@fastlane.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 02 Nov 2028 12:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Deployment mode follow-up — latency & throughput thresholds

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. We’re aligned on the numbers; the CSV you attached matches our internal capture. Two quick clarifying questions before we commit to a Dedicated microbench:

1) Cost delta: can Hosted be tuned (aggressive batching + prefix/KV caching) to meet p99 <= 250ms for most of our traffic at materially lower cost than Dedicated? We understand there are tradeoffs, just want a directional ballpark so procurement can compare.
2) SLA/rollback: if we start Hosted and see p99 slippage, what’s the expected lead time to move traffic to Dedicated?

Procurement note: we’d like to keep Private VPC as a contingency; current priority is minimizing TCO while hitting SLAs. We can share a 2-hour raw request log (timestamps + token counts) by end of day.

Ethan Shaw
Head of Platform, FastLane Analytics
ethan@fastlane.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Shaw <ethan@fastlane.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 02 Nov 2028 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Deployment mode follow-up — latency & throughput thresholds

Ethan — good questions. Short answers here, followed by the pilot detail we’d run.

- Can Hosted be tuned to meet p99? Possibly for infrequent bursts. Hosted’s smart batching and prefix/KV caching deliver large wins on token cost and average latency. However, p99 tail under sustained, multi-minute 350 qps bursts will likely exceed 250ms on Hosted because of queueing and shared instance contention; we’d expect variability.

- Lead time to move from Hosted to Dedicated: operationally we can route traffic to a Dedicated pool within minutes once capacity is provisioned; provisioning a new Dedicated pool (if you don’t already reserve capacity) can take 24–72 hours depending on sizing and availability. Canarying traffic is straightforward — we can do weighted routing (10% -> 90%) during a validation window.

Proposed microbench (details):
- Phase A (48h): Replay your 2-hour trace repeatedly over a Dedicated pool sized to mimic a 350 qps burst pattern. Measure p50/p95/p99 and sustained utilization.
- Phase B (24h concurrent): Run the same traffic against a Hosted tuning config (aggressive batching + prefix cache + reduced sequence window) to observe delta on p99 and cost.
- Deliverables: latency histograms, token cost estimates, autoscale behavior, and a recommended rollout sequence (Hosted fallback rules vs immediate Dedicated cutover).

If you can share the 2-hour trace, we’ll draft a short SOW for the microbench and a pilot pricing estimate. Proposed pilot start: Tue, Nov 7.

Next call: Fri Nov 9, 11:00 AM PT to review SOW and pilot pricing. Let me know if that works.

—Marissa
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 03 Nov 2028 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Deployment mode follow-up — latency & throughput thresholds (FastLane FLA-031)

Looping you in on FLA-031 — they’re sending a 2-hour trace and want a Dedicated microbench + Hosted tuning comparison. Quick pricing thought: for a 2–4 week committed pilot I recommend we offer a pilot credit to remove friction; propose the following band:
- Pilot credit: up to $12k applied to pilot usage (covers Dedicated baseline + benching hours)
- If customer signs a 3-month reserved commit within 30 days post-pilot, convert pilot credit into a 30% commitment credit applied to first invoice.

Why: reduces procurement friction and keeps margin intact if they convert. We’ll need ops to pre-allocate a small Dedicated pool for benching; Marissa flagged Tue, Nov 7 as a start.

Can you approve the pilot credit and the conversion term? If yes I’ll include this in the SOW draft and send to procurement.

Ben
